The core signal logic depends on a custom indicator that must be manually reimplemented in Python. Position open/close functions are from the external .mqh, not standard MT5 API.

derived_values.name: UpValue - buy signal from KaufWMAcross buffer 1
derived_values.formula: KaufWMAcross buffer[1] at SignalBar: non-zero and not EMPTY_VALUE = AMA crosses above LWMA

derived_values.name: DnValue - sell signal from KaufWMAcross buffer 0
derived_values.formula: KaufWMAcross buffer[0] at SignalBar: non-zero and not EMPTY_VALUE = AMA crosses below LWMA

derived_values.name: Historical close signal for existing position
derived_values.formula: Scan bars from SignalBar+1 to Bars()-1 for opposite signal in buffer 0 or 1 to set BUY_Close/SELL_Close when both open and close flags are enabled
derived_values.used_by: exit rule (signal reversal close with confirmation)

other_exits: When both BuyPosOpen and BuyPosClose (or SellPosOpen and SellPosClose) are true and no close signal on current bar, the EA scans historical bars from SignalBar+1 onward for a prior opposite signal to set close flags. This is a retroactive confirmation check to avoid closing when the cross happened too recently to have an open position.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMMode enum selects between free margin fraction, balance fraction, loss-adjusted free margin, loss-adjusted balance, or fixed lot. Current default is LOT (fixed lot of 0.1).

custom_logic_notes: The EA uses a Kaufman AMA vs LWMA crossover system via the custom 'KaufWMAcross' indicator (2 buffers: buffer 0 = down/sell crossover dots, buffer 1 = up/buy crossover dots, EMPTY_VALUE when no signal). It includes a retroactive position-check: when both entry and exit are enabled for a direction, but no exit signal fires on SignalBar, it scans backward through bars to find if an opposite signal exists, ensuring there was actually a position opened before trying to close it. The #include <TradeAlgorithms.mqh> provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, and LoadHistory — all must be reimplemented. The signal bar defaults to 1 (previous completed bar), avoiding repainting.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement Kaufman AMA indicator: er = abs(close - close[ama_period]) / sum(abs(close[i] - close[i-1]) for i in range(1, ama_period+1)); fast_sc = 2/(fast_ma_period+1); slow_sc = 2/(slow_ma_period+1); sc = (er*(fast_sc - slow_sc) + slow_sc)^2; ama = ama_prev + sc*(close - ama_prev). Then compute LWMA(period=13) on close. Entry: AMA crosses above LWMA = long; AMA crosses below LWMA = short. StopLoss=1000 points, TakeProfit=2000 points. Signal on bar[1] (previous bar), execute at next bar open. The retroactive position-check logic can be simplified in Python by tracking whether a position was actually opened before sending a close order. MarginMode=LOT means fixed lot sizing at 0.1 lots.
